title: Guaranteed delivery, idempotency and message ordering

videos.script: A broker promises to deliver your message. This lesson is about what that promise is worth. {{promise}} There are three kinds of promise, and the names sound better than they are. At most once. At least once. Exactly once. {{three}} The one you nearly always get is at least once. It means the message arrives, and sometimes it arrives twice. {{twice}} On your machine you will charge a customer twice, with a consumer that crashes at the worst possible moment. {{crash}} Then you will make the same crash harmless, by teaching the consumer to recognise a message it has already handled. That is idempotency, and it is the most useful word in this course. {{idempotent}} You will look at the other end too. A publisher that finds out when its message went nowhere. An order and its message that are saved together or not at all. {{outbox}} And you will meet the message that fails every time, and give it somewhere to go other than back to the front of the queue. {{poison}} Ordering gets its own section, because it is the promise most often assumed and least often kept.
